interface.name: mcpbrowser_dmabuf_capture_manager_v1

description.summary: leased output buffers without a capture blit

interface.description: Private local protocol. A frame leases the actual committed output buffer. The compositor MUST NOT recycle it until the client destroys the frame. A client must finish all GPU reads before destroying the frame. No CPU image transfer or second render target is involved.

request.name: capture

description.summary: lease the next damaged output commit

request.description: force=1 asks the compositor for one initial/current frame. force=0 waits for real output damage and does not schedule a repaint. At most four outstanding frame objects per session are allowed.

event.name: cursor_position

description.summary: cursor metadata kept out of the video framebuffer

event.description: x/y are logical output pixels. visible=0 hides the client overlay. Cursor motion never schedules an output repaint in the private direct KWin backend.

event.name: cursor_shape
event.description: shape is the freedesktop cursor-shape name when available. Surface cursors report default; the video client may use its local equivalent.

description.summary: explicit acquire sync_file, when supplied by renderer

event.name: damage

description.summary: device-pixel region changed since the preceding output commit

event.description: The event may be repeated. A forced/current frame is reported as full output damage so a consumer can initialize a persistent conversion surface without a separate copy.

event.name: failed

description.summary: no buffer was leased; destroy this frame

event.description: 1=output gone, 2=unsupported buffer/crop, 3=too many leases, 4=acquire fence could not be exported, 5=session destroyed.
